name: Amazon Aurora (PostgreSQL and MySQL compatible)
model: Tables of rows with SQL; speaks the PostgreSQL or the MySQL protocol and dialect (you pick one per cluster)
engine_note: Postgres or MySQL (InnoDB) query engine on top of a shared, log-structured storage volume kept in copies across three Availability Zones
consistency: Same transaction semantics as the engine it is compatible with (Postgres: read committed default, serializable option; MySQL: repeatable read default). Commits are durable in the multi-AZ storage volume. Reader replicas share storage but lag, usually under 100 ms, so replica reads can be stale.
scaling: One writer plus up to 15 readers on shared storage that grows automatically (up to 256 TiB); Serverless v2 resizes compute; Global Database for other regions; Limitless Database shards Postgres writes.
version_note: Aurora PostgreSQL 18.6 released 2026-09-29; newest Aurora MySQL is version 3.13.0 (2026-08-27, compatible with MySQL 8.0.45).
reach: Reach for it when you want Postgres or MySQL on AWS with fast failover, many read replicas and storage you never resize by hand.
avoid: Avoid when you need to run outside AWS, want the newest community Postgres or MySQL major on day one, or are cost sensitive at small scale.
escape: Adds storage copied across three zones, fast failover, up to 15 readers and auto-growing storage over Postgres.
chat: Users, chats and messages, as with Postgres or MySQL, when the product already lives on AWS.
notes: No Jepsen analysis of Aurora exists. Jepsen's 2025-04-29 RDS for PostgreSQL 17.4 report tested RDS Multi-AZ DB clusters (a different product: community Postgres with two readable standbys), not Aurora; Jepsen's 2023-12-19 MySQL 8.0.34 report tested RDS MySQL, also not Aurora. Neither finding should be read as an Aurora result. The 'six copies, four-of-six write quorum' design is from the 2017 SIGMOD Aurora paper; current docs say only 'copies across three Availability Zones', so the number is not stated in the row. Aurora DSQL (a separate serverless distributed SQL service, GA 2025) is a different product and not covered here. Aurora MySQL version 3 tracks MySQL 8.0; no Aurora MySQL 8.4-compatible major was listed on the release-notes page read 2026-10-04 (unconfirmed whether one exists elsewhere).
